  - VC-2: The conversation_id used in the suffix is the same id the agent received (the server-minted one passed into query_database_impl_with_widgets and send_message), not one the agent re-mints. [src/sqllens/server.py]
  - VC-3: _agent_error_result's text 'Error executing tool query_database: <message>' is byte-identical to what FastMCP produces when the tool re-raises. [src/sqllens/server.py]
  - VC-4: FastMCP passes a returned CallToolResult (with isError and _meta) through to the client unchanged rather than wrapping it. [src/sqllens/server.py]
  - VC-5: pydantic-settings parses SQLLENS_AGENT__SHOW_CONVERSATION_FOOTER='false' to boolean False for the nested agent model. [src/sqllens/config.py]
  - VC-6: The comment asserts the memory-unavailable path and other AgentRunError messages without the tail are unaffected; the server docstring says the conversation id is returned on every isError result built by _agent_error_result. [src/sqllens/server.py]
  - VC-7: The internal doc says with the footer off the id reaches the client only through _meta, covering both success and error text. [docs/internal/mcp-server/tools.md]
  - VC-8: Test helpers _agent, _GatedRunSql, _TOOL_PROMPT (test_query_database_tool_history) and _model_info, _query_database_fn, _StubCtx (test_server) exist with the signatures used, and agent.tool_registry.execute is the method the real Agent calls to run a tool. [tests/unit/test_conversation_footer_setting.py]
  - VC-9: fake_impl's keyword signature and 5-tuple return match query_database_impl_with_widgets as called by server.py. [tests/unit/test_conversation_footer_setting.py]
  - VC-10: Setting agent.agent_memory.open_error makes the real path raise AgentRunError with _MEMORY_UNAVAILABLE_MESSAGE. [tests/unit/test_conversation_footer_setting.py]
  - VC-11: The test's _FOOTER constant matches append_conversation_footer's exact output. [tests/unit/test_conversation_footer_setting.py]
  - VC-12: `AgentRuntimeConfig` has a boolean field `show_conversation_footer` whose default is `true`. A config without the field loads with `true`; `[agent] show_conversation_footer = false` in TOML and `SQLLENS_AGENT__SHOW_CONVERSATION_FOOTER=false` in the environment each load it as `false`; the environment value wins over the TOML value. The `[agent]` block of the `sqllens init` config template (`_SAMPLE_CONFIG` in `src/sqllens/cli.py`) carries a commented `show_conversation_footer` line naming its default and the env override. [src/sqllens/config.py]
  - VC-13: With the setting `true`, every `query_database` result kind in the Desired Behavior table (success, agent-run failure with a trace, agent-run failure with no trace, any other failure) has the same text, `isError` value and `_meta` as before this change, byte for byte, and an agent-run failure with no trace is still raised rather than returned. [src/sqllens/server.py]
  - VC-14: With the setting `false`, a successful `query_database` result's text is the answer with no conversation-ID footer, and its `_meta` holds the same keys and values it holds with the setting `true`, including `_meta["sqllens/conversation"]["conversation_id"]`. [src/sqllens/server.py]
  - VC-15: With the setting `false`, every `AgentRunError` that `query_database_impl_with_widgets` raises, with or without a trace, comes back as a returned `isError` result whose text is `Error executing tool query_database: ` followed by the error message with the conversation-ID tail (`"\n\nConversation ID: " + <the request's conversation id>`) removed from its end, and whose `_meta` holds `sqllens/conversation` with that conversation id, plus `sqllens/agent_trace` only when the error carries a trace. A message that does not end with that tail, such as the memory-store-unavailable message or a `Tool failed: …` message from a SQL statement a guard blocked, keeps its text unchanged. [src/sqllens/server.py]
  - VC-16: With the setting `false`, no `query_database` response text, success or error, contains conversation-ID text that SQL Lens adds: neither the footer nor the conversation-ID tail. Text the model writes into its answer is not filtered, so an answer that quotes an ID keeps it. [src/sqllens/server.py]
  - VC-17: The change leaves the failures not raised as `AgentRunError` (for example the internal-error `RuntimeError` or an invalid profile name) as they are today, raised with no conversation ID in text or `_meta`, whatever the setting. It leaves the rest of the error wording unchanged (the `Error executing tool query_database:` prefix, the `SQL execution error:` prefix and the error card's sentence) and leaves the vendored `src/sqllens/agent/core/agent/agent.py` unchanged. [src/sqllens/server.py]
  - VC-18: The `query_database` tool description no longer says the conversation ID is always in a plain-text footer: it says the ID is returned in `_meta["sqllens/conversation"]` and also as a text footer unless the server's `show_conversation_footer` setting is off. [src/sqllens/server.py]
  - VC-19: Tests cover both setting values on the success path and on agent-run failures with and without a trace, and assert the result text and `_meta` for each. The agent-run failure tests run the real vendored `Agent` so that its catch-all handler in `src/sqllens/agent/core/agent/agent.py` produces the error card and its conversation-ID tail; a stub that copies the card's text, or a hand-built `AgentRunError`, does not meet this criterion on its own. [tests/unit/test_conversation_footer_setting.py]

  </details>

acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `AgentRuntimeConfig` has a boolean field `show_conversation_footer` whose default is `true`. A config without the field loads with `true`; `[agent] show_conversation_footer = false` in TOML and `SQLLENS_AGENT__SHOW_CONVERSATION_FOOTER=false` in the environment each load it as `false`; the environment value wins over the TOML value. The `[agent]` block of the `sqllens init` config template (`_SAMPLE_CONFIG` in `src/sqllens/cli.py`) carries a commented `show_conversation_footer` line naming its default and the env override.
- [ ] With the setting `true`, every `query_database` result kind in the Desired Behavior table (success, agent-run failure with a trace, agent-run failure with no trace, any other failure) has the same text, `isError` value and `_meta` as before this change, byte for byte, and an agent-run failure with no trace is still raised rather than returned.
- [ ] With the setting `false`, a successful `query_database` result's text is the answer with no conversation-ID footer, and its `_meta` holds the same keys and values it holds with the setting `true`, including `_meta["sqllens/conversation"]["conversation_id"]`.
- [ ] With the setting `false`, every `AgentRunError` that `query_database_impl_with_widgets` raises, with or without a trace, comes back as a returned `isError` result whose text is `Error executing tool query_database: ` followed by the error message with the conversation-ID tail (`"\n\nConversation ID: " + <the request's conversation id>`) removed from its end, and whose `_meta` holds `sqllens/conversation` with that conversation id, plus `sqllens/agent_trace` only when the error carries a trace. A message that does not end with that tail, such as the memory-store-unavailable message or a `Tool failed: …` message from a SQL statement a guard blocked, keeps its text unchanged.
- [ ] With the setting `false`, no `query_database` response text, success or error, contains conversation-ID text that SQL Lens adds: neither the footer nor the conversation-ID tail. Text the model writes into its answer is not filtered, so an answer that quotes an ID keeps it.
- [ ] The change leaves the failures not raised as `AgentRunError` (for example the internal-error `RuntimeError` or an invalid profile name) as they are today, raised with no conversation ID in text or `_meta`, whatever the setting. It leaves the rest of the error wording unchanged (the `Error executing tool query_database:` prefix, the `SQL execution error:` prefix and the error card's sentence) and leaves the vendored `src/sqllens/agent/core/agent/agent.py` unchanged.
- [ ] The `query_database` tool description no longer says the conversation ID is always in a plain-text footer: it says the ID is returned in `_meta["sqllens/conversation"]` and also as a text footer unless the server's `show_conversation_footer` setting is off.
- [ ] Tests cover both setting values on the success path and on agent-run failures with and without a trace, and assert the result text and `_meta` for each. The agent-run failure tests run the real vendored `Agent` so that its catch-all handler in `src/sqllens/agent/core/agent/agent.py` produces the error card and its conversation-ID tail; a stub that copies the card's text, or a hand-built `AgentRunError`, does not meet this criterion on its own.
